fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says the seven lamps “…are to light the area in front of the lampstand.” Seven little flames, and every one of them has a job: point forward and light up the work. Aaron does exactly that, setting them up facing toward the front, just as the LORD had commanded Moses (Numbers 8:3). I once got called out of a junk drawer for a job, so I know the feeling of being handed a clear assignment and wanting to get it right.

Good try, friend, but moving isn't the first thing the LORD asks. He says, “Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.” The text does have them brought before the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 8:9), but cleansing is where the LORD starts, and it's the first thing on His list. Step one is the washing, not the moving.

That's right, baker. The text says the Levites came to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting “…in the presence of Aaron and his sons.” Moses and the elders are a nice guess, but they aren't named in that verse. Think of it like a first day on the job where you're working right next to the people in charge. Then the verse wraps up by saying they did with the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses (Numbers 8:22).

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “…at the age of fifty, they must retire from performing the work and no longer serve.” Fifty is the line, and the verse says must. Now hold your hats, because retirement isn't the end of the story. Verse 26 says they “…may assist their brothers in fulfilling their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they themselves are not to do the work.” So no more heavy lifting, but they're still around to lend a hand (Numbers 8:26).
